purpose: Everything needed to recreate the H3 environment on a different host. The OLD pod ufhtfdg9ulv3fj is kept EXITED as insurance and must not be deleted or modified.

old_pod.name: h3-clipcached-baseline
old_pod.note: DELETED 2026-09-07 on the operator's instruction, along with four other unused Pods. The id is kept for provenance; pod_migrate.sh no longer describes it -- it refuses when ANY Pod is RUNNING instead, which does not break when the pile changes.

recreate_spec.name: h3-clipcached-baseline-3
recreate_spec.imageName_note: MUST match. The venv at /workspace/ComfyUI/.venv was built by this image's interpreter (Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04.4, GCC 13.3.0). A different image with a different Python minor version breaks it.
gpuTypeIds: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
recreate_spec.dataCenterIds_note: forced: network volume olmj77x4pc lives in US-WA-1 and can only attach to a pod in the same data center.
recreate_spec.gpuTypeIds_note: Ordered by preference: the baseline RTX 6000 Ada first, then other 48 GB cards, then larger. 48 GB is the floor because the measured cache-MISS peak is 47.3 GiB. If a non-Ada card is used, absolute times and VRAM are NOT comparable to the baseline measurements -- only the A/B/C comparison among themselves is.
recreate_spec.env_note: PUBLIC_KEY is injected by RunPod from the account SSH keys; not set by us
recreate_spec.allowedCudaVersions_note: OMITTED ON PURPOSE - requiring 13.0 returns 'no instances currently available' even on machines reporting CUDA 13.0

measured_requirements.peak_vram_note: 47.3 GiB observed on a 49140 MiB card during a cache MISS, when the 27 GB Qwen3-VL encoder is resident. Cache HIT runs peak at ~26 GiB. 48 GB is the validated size; do not go below it.

persistence_audit.verdict: everything required lives on the network volume
not_on_volume_but_reproduced_by_the_imag: system python 3.12.3 and OS packages (from imageName)
NVIDIA driver / CUDA runtime (from the host + image)
persistence_audit.nothing_else_installed_outside_workspace: install_comfyui.sh only creates the venv under /workspace/ComfyUI and pip-installs into it; no apt-get, no system-wide installs.

availability_survey_us_wa_1_secure.verdict: FIRST CHOICE - identical to the validated baseline
fallback - 80 GB is ample, sm_80 is supported by torch cu130, but it is a different architecture than the one the baseline was measured on

rejected_candidates: Every other GPU type in US-WA-1 SECURE returned no price and no stock, i.e. not purchasable right now. Community cloud has none. Anything under 48 GB was excluded on the measured 47.3 GiB peak.
